headline: Kept Boynton Yards zoning change and four housing amendments in committee after public hearings on backyard cottages and affordable units.
summary: Nick Barker presented an amended Boynton Yards plan that would raise the minimal allowable from 25% to 40%, citing a rising need for housing. Three residents spoke in favor, while others raised concerns about fewer commercial spaces and the loss of arts spaces. Eight residents spoke on the affordable housing and backyard cottage amendments, and written comments are accepted until November 13, 2026.
decisions: Kept in committee the Boynton Yards zoning text amendment to Section 8.4.12.e.ii.
Kept in committee the zoning text amendment regarding affordable dwelling units in Section 12.1.2.
Kept in committee the zoning text amendment to Zoning Board of Appeals board rules in Section 15.7.2.d.
Kept in committee the zoning text amendment on backyard cottages in Section 3.1.12 (ID 26-1510).
Kept in committee the zoning text amendment on backyard cottages in Section 3.1.12 (ID 26-1509).

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Land Use Committee Meeting Minutes

Thursday, November 5, 2026

6:30 PM

Joint Meeting with the Planning Board

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Ewen-Campen at 6:33 PM and adjourned at 8:09 PM on a roll call vote of 4 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, Ewen-Campen), 0 opposed, and 1 absent (Councilor McLaughlin).

The Council went into recess from 6:33 PM and returned at 6:35 PM on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin, Ewen-Campen).

Councilor McLaughlin left the meeting at 7:24 PM.

Others present: Amelia Aboff - Vice Chair of the Planning Board, Coralie Cooper – Planning Board Member, Jahan Habib – Planning Board Member, Lynn Richards – Planning Board Member, Luc Shuscter – Planning Board Member, Michael McNeeley – Planning Board Member, Michael Capuano – Chair of Planning Board, Madalyn Letellier – Assistant City Clerk, Legislative Services.

Roll Call

- Present: Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis, Ward Four City
- Councilor Jesse Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Naima
- Sait, Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin and
- Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen

1. Public Hearings

1.1. Public

Boynton Yards LandCo LLC and Windsor Place Owner LLC requesting a

Communication Zoning Text Amendment to amend section 8.4.12.e.ii.

(ID # 26-1480 )

Nick Barker presented on the amended plan, Land Use 2026-11-05 Boynton

Yards Amendment (with 261480). He explained the need for housing has

- risen while life sciences has slowed, increased minimal allowable from 25%

to 40% to allow for flexibility in housing and preserving the mixed use intention for Boynton Yards.

Chair Ewen-Campen opened the public hearing at 6:45 PM.

Three residents spoke in favor of the change, and one encouraged the developers to partner with permanent-supportive housing resources. One

resident shared concern that other developers want to make changes to the zoning to residential and wonders will be lost with fewer commercial

- spaces. Another resident shared concerns over loss of arts spaces.

- There being no further speaker’s Chair Ewen-Campen closed the public
- hearing at 6:56 PM. Comments will be accepted until Friday November 13,

2026, at 12:00 PM and can be submitted to publiccomments@somervillema.gov.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

1.2. Public

36 registered voters requesting a Zoning Text Amendment to amend Zoning

Communication Ordinance Section 12.1.2 regarding affordable dwelling units.

(ID # 26-1512 )

Bill White spoke to all four agenda items together, #26-1512, #26-1511, #26-1510, and #26-1509, as they align in context. He highlighted one takes

away the ZBA’s ability to enact rules and regulations, there is an amendment related to space in backyard cottage, and a language amendment to prevent

backyard cottages from being a free-standing condo unit. All four are as a result from the concern that if more is built the price will go down, which

Mr. White does not agree with. He spoke to the potential of displacing residents for individuals who can afford to live in a luxury condominium.

Chair Ewen-Campen opened the public hearing at 7:23 PM.

- Eight residents spoke to the four amendments in front of the body. On

resident urged the Council to be considerate of the housing that is near the developments. One resident spoke in favor of the amendments before the body and asked that the city rethink its zoning approach. Two residents

expressed disappointment in the lack of notice for hearings and taking votes on items before a public comment period has ended and urged the body to consider the choices being made around affordability and lot splits and not

make decisions in a hurry. One resident spoke specifically to the three foot dimension and the lack of affordability requirements.

- There being no further speaker’s Chair Ewen-Campen closed the public
- hearing at 8:06 PM. Comments will be accepted until Friday November 13,

2026, at 12:00 PM and can be submitted to publiccomments@somervillema.gov.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE
